title: Grove reserves abstention for pre-disclosed conflicts of interest and treats every other abstention as non-performance
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.3.3 requires a Delegate to "cast a vote on **every** governance proposal within the designated voting window," and states that "failure to achieve this may result in non-eligibility for payment or offboarding." A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.3.4 then narrows the alternative: "The 'Abstain' option may be used **solely** in cases where the Delegate has a documented conflict of interest for the specific proposal." A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.3.4.1 requires the conflict to be disclosed to the Grove Foundation *before* the voting window opens, and A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.3.4.2 makes abstaining for any other reason "non-performance" under the offboarding provisions.

Abstention has been repurposed. In most voting systems it means "present but not choosing" — a signal of uncertainty, insufficient information, or deliberate neutrality. Here it means exactly one thing: **recusal for a declared conflict**. The signal is stripped of ambiguity and reused as a compliance marker.

The gain is that the abstain tally becomes readable. A delegate abstaining tells the reader a conflict exists and was disclosed in advance, which is a genuinely useful fact and one that an ordinary abstain option destroys by pooling recusals with indifference. The prior-disclosure requirement is what secures it: a conflict declared before the window cannot be invented afterwards to excuse a missed vote.

The cost is that a delegate with no view must still choose. Someone who has read a proposal and honestly concludes they lack the expertise to judge it has no compliant way to say so — voting either way misrepresents their state of knowledge, and abstaining is punishable. The framework has decided that a forced position is preferable to an ambiguous non-position.

That pressure is partly offset by A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.3.5, which requires "a concise rationale for each vote on the proposal thread." Participation is what gets enforced by pay and offboarding; the written rationale is the only check on whether the participation was considered. Where the measurable duty is attendance, the unmeasured one is judgement.
description: Delegates must vote on every proposal and may abstain only with a conflict disclosed to the Foundation before the voting window;
